description: **CAM7 – Community Atmosphere Model version 7**  CAM7 is the atmospheric general circulation model of CESM3, developed at the NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research together with the CAM community. It simulates the resolved dynamics of the atmosphere together with parameterized turbulence, convection, clouds, precipitation, radiation, gravity-wave drag and aerosols, and is the successor to CAM6 (CESM2). CAM7 is available in two vertical configurations: a **Mid-Top (MT)** configuration extending from the surface into the upper mesosphere (~80 km) and a **Low-Top (LT)** configuration extending to the upper stratosphere (~42 km); see Section 1.  **Chemistry and aerosols:** CAM7 can be run in two chemistry configurations that share the same dynamics and physics:  - **T4S (default for CMIP7):** Interactive troposphere–stratosphere chemistry for climate simulations from the MOZART chemical mechanism suite. The tropospheric mechanism includes detailed oxidation pathways for O<sub>3</sub>, NO<sub>x</sub>, HO<sub>x</sub>, methane (CH<sub>4</sub>), carbon monoxide (CO), and other non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs), which interact with the aerosol scheme. Aerosols are represented by the five-mode Modal Aerosol Module (MAM5), which adds a stratospheric sulfate mode to MAM4. Additional shortwave heating is included at high altitudes due to photolysis of O<sub>2</sub> and O<sub>3</sub> by solar ultraviolet radiation. This includes both the direct thermal heating and chemical potential heating. The additional shortwave heating is merged with the shortwave heating at lower altitudes between 50 and 5 Pa. This configuration is used for the CMIP7 spin-up and production simulations.  - **SO (specified oxidants):** Limited interactive gas-phase chemistry in the troposphere, mostly for tropospheric aerosol representation, including sulfate and organic aerosol; oxidant fields are prescribed from the T4S simulation, greenhouse-gas concentrations are prescribed at the model surface, and some loss rates are included for H<sub>2</sub>O and methane. Stratospheric ozone and aerosols are prescribed from the T4S simulations. Aerosols are represented by the four-mode Modal Aerosol Module (MAM4). This configuration is intended for applications where the cost of full chemistry is not justified.  Both configurations include cloud-droplet activation and ice nucleation from the aerosol population, and aerosol optical properties are computed assuming internally mixed lognormal modes.
1._grids_and_dynamical_core: **Horizontal grid.** The standard 1° configuration (`ne30pg3`) uses the spectral-element (SE) dynamical core on a cubed-sphere grid of 30 × 30 elements per face, each with 4 × 4 Gauss–Lobatto–Legendre nodes (~110 km nominal resolution). Tracer transport uses the Conservative Semi-Lagrangian Multi-tracer scheme (CSLAM), and the physics parameterizations and model output are on a separate quasi-equal-area finite-volume grid of 3 × 3 cells per element (48,600 columns globally). This SE-CSLAM configuration is described in Lauritzen et al. (2017, 2018) and Herrington et al. (2018). Variable-resolution SE grids (without a separate physics grid and CSLAM tracer transport) are also supported. *Horizontal discretization of the `ne30pg3` grid: (a) six cubed-sphere faces, (b) 30 × 30 spectral elements per face, (c) the 4 × 4 GLL dynamics grid and the 3 × 3 physics/output grid within one element.* **Vertical grid.** A hybrid sigma–dry-pressure (dry-mass) coordinate replaces the moist hybrid-sigma coordinate of earlier CAM versions; condensate mass is included in the total pressure. Two vertical grids are offered, both registered in the EMD: - **Mid-Top (MT, default):** 93 levels, model top near 80 km (~0.4 Pa) in the upper mesosphere. The stratosphere is resolved with ~500 m spacing, sufficient to internally generate a QBO. EMD vertical grid [`v162`](https://github.com/WCRP-CMIP/Essential-Model-Documentation/blob/src-data/vertical_computational_grid/v162.json). - **Low-Top (LT):** 58 levels, model top near 42 km (~2 hPa) in the upper stratosphere, similar in extent to CAM6 but with the CAM7 boundary-layer refinement; intended for applications where a resolved stratosphere is not required. EMD vertical grid [`v163`](https://github.com/WCRP-CMIP/Essential-Model-Documentation/blob/src-data/vertical_computational_grid/v163.json). Both roughly double the number of levels below 800 hPa relative to CAM6 (~16 levels, layer thickness < 200 m), with the lowest model level at ~20 m. Both share the `ne30pg3` horizontal grid, registered as EMD horizontal computational grid [`h149`](https://github.com/WCRP-CMIP/Essential-Model-Documentation/blob/src-data/horizontal_computational_grid/h149.json) (grid cell [`g231`](https://github.com/WCRP-CMIP/Essential-Model-Documentation/blob/src-data/horizontal_grid_cell/g231.json)). *Layer thickness versus height for CAM6 (32 levels), CAM7-LT (58) and CAM7-MT (93): (a) full column, (b) lowest 2 km.* **Spectral-Element Dynamical-core updates since CESM2.2** include orography-based reference profiles for hyperviscosity, an Exner-form pressure-gradient force, a generalized thermodynamic / major-species infrastructure, coupling with the CSLAM transport scheme, and updated topography generation (NCAR Topo) software with internal Laplacian smoothing (https://github.com/NCAR/Topo) so that the Topo software is dynamical-core agnostic. The **Model for Prediction Across Scales (MPAS; https://github.com/MPAS-Dev/MPAS-Model/)** dynamical core is also supported in CAM7/CESM3 and is, in particular, used for kilometer-scale (~3.75 km) simulations.
2._physics_parameterizations: | Process | CAM7 scheme | |---|---| | Boundary layer, shallow convection, cloud macrophysics | Cloud Layers Unified By Binormals (CLUBB) is a prognostic, moist turbulence model that uses a double-Gaussian representation of the sub-grid state to close higher-order moments. In CAM7, CLUBB has been extended to include prognostic momentum fluxes and to operate above the tropopause, up to 100 Pa | | Deep convection | The Zhang and McFarlane (1995) deep convection scheme, with the Neale et al. (2008) modifications, is largely unchanged from CAM6 and uses a bulk-plume mass-flux approximation that consumes CAPE over a specified time scale. CAM7 includes an initial parcel calculation that is now a function of the boundary layer depth and a parallel conservative boundary layer moist static energy mixing. This reduces the sensitivity to vertical grid spacing seen with the previous configuration | | Unified Boundary layer, shallow convection, cloud macrophysics and deep convection | CLUBB-MF is CLUBB coupled to a mass-flux (MF) plume scheme (essentially a unified deep-shallow convection scheme) used for km-scale configurations of CAM7 | | Stratiform microphysics | PUMAS (two-moment successor to MG2) with updated ice-number limiter and ice nucleation | | LTE Radiation | RTE+RRTMGP is a modern k-distribution radiative transfer scheme (which assumes Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium - LTE) that CAM7 uses as its default longwave and shortwave radiation parameterization. In CAM's implementation it is driven through an interface that maps a fixed set of 8 gases (H2O, O3, O2, CO2, N2O, CH4, CFC11, CFC12) onto either prognostic model fields or prescribed datasets, and it couples to cloud and aerosol optics | | non-LTE Radiation | From ~50 Pa to ~5 Pa the LTE (Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium) radiation scheme (i.e. RRTMGP) transitions smoothly to the non-LTE radiation scheme of Fomichev et al. (1998) | | Gravity waves / drag | Beljaars orographic form drag, anisotropic orographic GW, convective (Beres) and frontal non-orographic GW, new low-phase-speed frontal ("moving mountains") source. Moving mountain source launches a single GW phase speed per gridbox-timestep, determined by tropospheric winds. This contrasts with the broad GW spectrum launched by the existing frontal scheme. The amplitude of the moving-mountain GWs is flow-dependent instead of a global constant as in the frontal scheme. For km-scale configurations of CAM7, gravity wave parameterizations are turned off | | Aerosols | MAM5 in the T4S configuration and MAM4 in the SO configuration, both with cloud-droplet activation and ice nucleation | | Chemistry | Extensive MOZART chemistry (T4S) or specified oxidants (SO) | *Evolution of CAM physics, dynamical cores and vertical grids from CAM4 to CAM7.*
3._notable_features_of_this_version: Relative to CAM6: raised model top and resolved stratosphere (enabling an internally generated QBO), doubled boundary-layer resolution, dry-mass vertical coordinate with condensate loading, separate physics grid with CSLAM transport, prognostic momentum fluxes in CLUBB, RTE-RRTMGP radiation with a transition to non-LTE longwave cooling (Fomichev et al. 1998) and additional shortwave heating from O₂ and O₃ photolysis in the upper mesosphere, updated PUMAS microphysics (with important bug fixes), and a new low-phase-speed frontal ("moving mountain") gravity-wave source. Removal of the CLUBB-top limiter and the extended RRTMGP temperature range allow stable simulation of very warm (hothouse) climates. CAM7 was tuned primarily in the coupled CESM3 system using both expert-guided and automated (QuadTune, perturbed-parameter ensemble) approaches; note that the CAM7 physics has therefore not been specifically tuned for AMIP-style (prescribed-SST) simulations.  A CAM7 overview paper is in preparation for JAMES (Lauritzen et al.); the reference DOI will be updated on publication.
